messages:
Maria Gomez: hey — running into a VPN/network issue on day 2. I can SSH to the bastion but kubectl to the dev cluster times out. MacBook M1, home LAN is 10.1.2.0/24. any ideas?

Oliver: do you get an actual kubectl error? how are you connecting (kubeconfig points to a 10.x address?)

Maria Gomez: yup kubeconfig points at 10.254.3.12:6443. here's what I ran:
```
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa ubuntu@bastion.redwood.local
kubectl get pods --context=dev
# error:
Unable to connect to the server: dial tcp 10.254.3.12:6443: i/o timeout
```
Also `ipconfig getifaddr en0` -> `10.1.2.14` — i'm guessing my home subnet overlaps with the internal routes.

Jake (eng-infra): yep, sounds like an overlapping-private-subnet + split-tunnel interaction. Our VPN is split by default and expects internal ranges (10.254.0.0/16, 172.16.x.x, etc.) to be routed via the VPN. If your laptop's local net uses the same prefixes, macOS will prefer the local route. Two quick workarounds: 
1) Port-forward the API through the bastion (fast):
```
ssh -L 6443:10.254.3.12:6443 ubuntu@bastion.redwood.local
# then in another shell:
KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config kubectl --server=https://127.0.0.1:6443 get ns
```
2) Add an ephemeral host route on macOS to force traffic for the cluster via the VPN interface (replace utunX with the vpn interface you see in `ifconfig`):
```
# find the utun interface first: ifconfig | grep -B3 utun
sudo route -n add -net 10.254.0.0/16 -interface utun2
```
I can help find the right interface if you paste `ifconfig` output.

Maria Gomez: trying option 1 now...

infra-oncall: if you prefer not to mess with routes, another short workaround is to change your home router's LAN subnet to 192.168.x.x (if you have admin access) or use your phone as a hotspot (phone NAT usually uses a different private range). For a longer-term fix, we can open an eng-infra ticket to allocate a specific route/NAT for your assigned IP, but that takes a bit of coordination.

Maria Gomez: port-forward worked! i can list pods now :tada: thanks all

Jake (eng-infra): awesome. please file a ticket with eng-infra and include your public IP and macOS version if you want us to pre-provision something for you. we'll also add a short note to the new-hires VPN doc about checking for overlapping private ranges. thanks for surfacing this.

Maria Gomez: quick question — is the ssh -L approach ok security-wise for day-to-day dev use, or should i avoid it for anything sensitive?

Oliver: fine for dev/debugging, but don't tunnel prod credentials or anything PCI/sensitive through a personal machine unless explicitly approved. If you need persistent secure access we can create a jump-hosting entry tied to your user and manage certs.

Maria Gomez: perfect, filing the ticket now and will update the onboarding doc if useful. thanks everyone :)
